newsitem.title: UK: Brent spreads actively traded, spot market thin.
newsitem.headline: Brent spreads actively traded, spot market thin.

text.p: October cash Brent markets continued to track crude futures which dipped over the afternoon on profit-taking from this morning's U.S./Iraq tension-driven gains, traders said.
They said physical play was thin but spread trade had been active with the Oct/Nov spread trading in line with futures.

The prompt paper spread firmed to trade up to October +80 cents in the morning on expectations of further U.S. air strikes against Iraq, dipped to 73 cents as futures fell on profit-taking and strengthened sharply again in late trade on news that Iraq had again fired on U.S. warplanes.
October Brent paper stood around 23.60/65 cents at 1554 GMT, still well below this morning's $24 plus highs.

CFDs followed a similar pattern, weakening sharply and then steadying as October Brent strengthened. Next week's dates valued around October Brent -20, with Sept 23-27 contracts steady at Nov Brent +43 cents.
Dated Brent stayed weak with sellers reporting no interest in cargoes loading in the Sept 19-22 window, despite reports of offers down to October -20 cents
Buyers saw Dated Brent at as low as October -30 cents but no firm bids were heard.
Traders said the narrowing Brent/WTI spread was dampening U.S. refiner interest for the North Sea benchmark.
The Oct Brent/WTI spread stood at 97 cents at 1546 GMT, down from $1.25 earlier in the week.
"We are not finding any buying interest at these levels," an equity holder said.
All three Brent cargoes due to turn wet on Thursday were kept from the paper chains ahead of the five o'clock deadline.
The cargoes, due to load Sept 27-29, were kept by Wall Street trader J.P. Morgan, trade sources said.
